name: Caro-Kann Defence
tagline: A rock-solid answer to 1.e4 with clear plans and no bad bishop.
description: A complete Caro-Kann repertoire for Black: 1.e4 c6 2.d4 d5, getting the light-squared bishop out before closing the centre. You meet the Advance with ...Bf5 and ...c5, the Classical with ...Bf5-g6 and a rock-solid set-up, the Exchange and Panov with active pieces against White's centre, and every common sideline with a simple plan. The positions are sound and easy to understand, and you learn how to punish the mistakes club players actually make.

chapters.name: Advance Variation
chapters.intro: After 3.e5 White has space, but Black has a clear target: the d4 pawn at the base of the chain. Black puts the bishop on f5 first, then plays ...e6 and ...c5, adding ...Nc6, ...Qb6 or ...Ne7-f5 to pile up on d4. If the f3-knight is d4's main defender, pinning or taking it with ...Bg4 is a recurring idea. Against the aggressive 4.Nc3 and 5.g4 (the Bayonet), Black must hit back at once with ...c5 and stop h4-h5 with ...h5. Remember: the bishop goes to g6 or h7, never into a trap on e4.

Because c6 backs up d5, Black keeps a solid pawn in the centre whatever White does next. } 3. e5 { The Advance. White gains space and takes f6 away from Black's knight, but the d4 pawn at the base of the chain becomes a target. } Bf5 { The key Caro-Kann idea: the light-squared bishop gets outside the pawn chain before ...e6. quiz.question: What is Black's main pawn break against the Advance?
options: ...c5, attacking the base of the chain on d4
quiz.explanation: The d4 pawn holds the whole chain together. ...c5, backed by ...Nc6 and ...Qb6, attacks it directly; if d4 falls, e5 becomes weak too.

chapters.name: Exchange Variation
chapters.intro: After 3.exd5 cxd5 the pawns are symmetrical, and the game is about piece activity. Black develops with ...Nc6 and ...Nf6, then brings the light-squared bishop to g4 before playing ...e6, so it never gets stuck behind the pawns. Next Black offers to trade White's strong f4-bishop with ...Bd6, castles, and uses the half-open c-file. A typical long-term plan is the minority attack ...b5-b4 to create a weak pawn on c3. If White plays slowly, the freeing break ...e5 is often possible.

chapters.name: Panov Attack
chapters.intro: The Panov Attack usually gives White an isolated pawn on d4 after cxd5 or ...dxc4. That pawn gives White space and active pieces, but it is also a long-term weakness. Black's recipe: blockade the square in front of it with a knight on d5, attack d4 with ...Nc6 and ...Bf6, and trade pieces, because every trade makes the isolated pawn weaker. If White instead closes the position with c5, Black attacks the c5-b4 chain with ...b6 and ...a5.

chapters.name: Classical Variation
chapters.intro: Against 3.Nc3 or 3.Nd2 Black takes on e4 and develops the bishop to f5 with tempo. White chases it with Ng3 and h4-h5; Black answers ...Bg6, ...h6 and ...Bh7, then trades it on d3. With pawns on c6 and e6 and pieces on d7, f6 and e7, Black's position is very solid. Later Black castles and frees the game with ...c5 or ...e5. Watch for tricks against White's early sidelines: Nc5 and Bd3 often leave a pawn or a piece loose.

chapters.name: Fantasy Variation
chapters.intro: With 3.f3 White props up e4 and dreams of a big pawn centre. Black stays solid with ...e6, keeping d5 strong, and develops the bishop to b4 to pin the c3-knight. Plans are ...c5 against d4, ...Ne7 and quick castling, and ...dxe4 when it opens lines for Black's pieces. Remember that f3 weakens the e1-h4 diagonal: ...Qh4+ tricks appear when White plays fxe4 carelessly. Also watch b2 after Be3: ...Qb6 often wins a pawn.

chapters.name: Anti-Caro Sidelines
chapters.intro: Many players avoid the main lines on move two. Against 2.Nc3 and 2.Nf3 Black plays ...d5 and, after Nf3 and Nc3, pins with ...Bg4, takes on f3 and builds a solid ...e6 and ...Nf6 set-up. Against 2.c4 Black plays ...d5 and wins the pawn back with ...Nf6xd5, often reaching Panov positions. Against the King's Indian set-up with 2.d3, Black takes the whole centre with ...d5 and ...e5. Many of these lines transpose into earlier chapters, so look for familiar positions.

quiz.question: What is Black's main plan against the Two Knights?
options: ...Bg4, taking on f3 and setting up ...e6 and ...Nf6
quiz.explanation: Pinning and taking the f3-knight develops the bishop before ...e6 and leaves White's queen on f3, where it can be harassed.

quiz.question: White plays a King's Indian Attack set-up. What is a good plan for Black?
quiz.explanation: White is playing slowly, so Black can claim the centre with pawns on d5 and e5 and develop with ...Bd6, ...Nf6 and ...O-O.
